items.title: Karmine Corp完成救赎之旅，捧起无畏契约 EMEA赛区第二阶段冠军奖杯

content.v: Karmine Corp 成功击败了 Team Liquid，在 VCT EMEA 第二赛段总决赛中以 3-1 的比分夺冠，这也是该俱乐部历史上首次捧起 VCT 奖杯。自 2024 年的 Kickoff 赛事（那是该组织上一次赢得 VCT 赛事，尽管当时并未颁发奖杯）以来，这支“蓝军”终于再次成为了 EMEA 赛区的王者。
这是 VCT 历史上最引人注目的赛季中期翻盘之一：KC 从第一赛段的 0-5 战绩、排名第 11-12 位，一跃成为第二赛段的总冠军。KC 在本届赛事中展现了绝对的统治力，他们在 Omega 分组赛以 4-1 的战绩位列头名，随后在季后赛中以 3-0 的完美战绩夺冠。现在，Karmine Corp 将以 EMEA 赛区头号种子的身份前往上海全球冠军赛（Champions）。

KC 充分利用了“双图封禁”的优势，去掉了 Split 和 Abyss。这两张地图不仅是 Team Liquid 目前英雄池中的强图，也是 KC 在第二赛段中一直表现犹豫的地图。最终系列赛在 KC 选择的 Sunset、TL 选择的 Ascent 以及 KC 选择的 Lotus 上进行。最终，KC 以 13-7 拿下 Sunset，13-6 拿下 Ascent，Liquid 以 13-7 赢下 Lotus，最后 KC 以 13-10 终结了 Summit。

在 Sunset 上，KC 沿用了惯用的 Omen-Viper 阵容，N4RRATE 和 LewN 分别使用他们拿手的 Chamber 和 Neon。与此同时，这是 Team Liquid 自 2025 年以来首次在该图上比赛。比赛初期，KC 在 Sunset 上显得更加游刃有余，通过出色的战术执行早早建立起 6-1 的领先优势。尽管此后 Liquid 奋起直追，将比分扳平为 6-6，但 KC 在防守端的表现更为出色。dos9 重现了他此前效力于 BOOM Esports 时的超神状态，带领队伍在进攻端打出了近乎完美的表现，以 13-7 终结了比赛。
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/jfpHzNbubkcwhnc.png
dos9 拿下四杀，帮助 KC 赢下经济局。
虽然 Sunset 对 KC 来说是预料之中的胜利，但 Ascent 则是对双方的严峻考验。两队在第二赛段中均未在 Ascent 上尝过败绩，且都有成熟的“双决斗”阵容。KC 选择了 Phoenix-Neon 组合，而 Liquid 则沿用了前一天击败 FUT Esports 时那套强势的 Phoenix-Jett 阵容。
KC 在防守方率先发难，尽管丢掉了两局手枪局，但仍以 8-4 的防守半场领先。在 Liquid 拿下下半场手枪局后，KC 凭借一波关键的五把 Classic 经济局翻盘，彻底扭转了局势，最终势如破竹地以 13-6 拿下该图。
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/IMFJAxbubkcwizm.png
顺便提一下，那是五把 Classic 手枪。
Lotus 曾被视为 Liquid 的半强图，也是 KC 的绝对强图，这里似乎成了 Liquid 最后的希望。虽然 Liquid 在第二赛段该图战绩为 4-3，但 KC 此前保持着 5-0 的全胜记录。在比赛中，Liquid 止住了颓势，将 KC 的进攻轮次限制在 5 分，并凭借 Kicks 和 kamo 各自贡献的 23 次击杀，以 13-7 扳回一城，将比赛拖入 Summit。
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/hRYqhnbubkcwlma.png
Kicks 在 Lotus 上势不可挡。
当比赛进入 Summit 时，让二追三的可能性开始浮现。KC 在这张图上此前两战皆负，其中一次就是输给了小组赛的 Liquid。Liquid 的进攻风格延续了他们在季后赛对阵 Enterprise Esports 时的策略：死磕 A 点。他们通过连续冲击 A 点，开局打出 7-0 的高潮。KC 在上半场末段艰难追回几分，半场结束时比分为 7-5。
下半场，KC 找回了状态，赢下手枪局和反经济局，追平了比分。在 LeWN 的犀利突破，以及 N4RRATE 和 SUYGETSU 对 Liquid 防线缝隙的精准打击下，KC 在进攻端展现了极佳的配合。
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/gjJjkibubkcwmur.png
LeWN 的表现极其锐利。
KC 稳步推进，通过完美的经济管理和终极技能分配，不仅拿到了赛点，更以 12-10 的比分锁定了 VCT EMEA 的冠军头衔。
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/lFAsJcbubkcwqib.png
“蓝军”终于成为了冠军。
dos9 被评为 OMODA 总决赛 MVP。他在前两张地图中贡献了全队最高的击杀数和评分，最终以 70 次击杀和 1.28 的评分领跑全场。N4RRATE 紧随其后，贡献了 67 次击杀和 1.16 的评分。

对于 KC 来说，这一路走来实属不易。从低谷到巅峰，全队经历了一段坎坷的征程。dos9 在去年随 BOOM Esports 经历 0-5 的失利后，终于捧起了职业生涯首座 VCT 奖杯；LeWN 在去年多次与全球舞台擦肩而过后，终于以赛区冠军的身份登顶；SUYGETSU 作为 无畏契约 职业赛场的老将，也拿下了自合作制前夕 Masters Copenhagen 后的首个冠军头衔。此外，主教练 ZE1SH 和 2024 年便加入 KC 的 Avez 也共同见证了这一历史时刻。
无畏契约
第一人称射击, 英雄联盟, 海外, 次世代游戏
在过去的二十年里，拳头游戏也面临着IP单一和扩张力不足的问题，迫切需要开发一款基于新IP的热门游戏...事实证明，他们成功做到了。现在，这款游戏甚至也要在射击手游市场分一杯羹。

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/OULDstbubkbbbqz.png
Playground Games 确认，神鬼寓言4 的主线剧情通关大约需要 20 小时。
神鬼寓言4
角色扮演, 奇幻

在 2026 年 Gamescom 期间的一次集体问答中，副游戏总监 Will Kennedy 和 Craig Littler 分享了这款定于 2027 年发售的奇幻角色扮演游戏（RPG）的预计时长。虽然 Xbox 和 Playground 表示 神鬼寓言4 将拥有足够丰富的内容让玩家尽情体验，但玩家无需为了看到演职员表而在主线剧情上耗费数百小时。
“我们有大约 15-20 小时的主线任务流程，以及大约 15-20 小时的支线任务和开放世界探索内容，”Kennedy 说道。
随着大型 RPG 不断占据市场，这个时长可能比部分玩家预期的要短。像 艾尔登法环：黑夜君临、巫师 3：狂猎 和 刺客信条：英灵殿 这样著名的开放世界游戏，其宏大的世界和主线任务往往需要玩家花费 50 小时甚至更久才能通关。对于 神鬼寓言4 来说并非如此，但老粉丝们可能早有预料。

根据 Howlongtobeat 的数据，2004 年原版 神鬼寓言4 的主线任务时长约为 12.5 小时。神鬼寓言4 2 的时长也不过 13 小时，而 神鬼寓言4 3 则略长，约为 13.5 小时。如果不出意外，明年的 神鬼寓言4 重启版将成为系列中流程最长的一作，其主线战役的长度几乎是原版游戏的两倍。
这并不意味着玩家无法沉浸在 神鬼寓言4 的奇幻世界中。Kennedy 承诺，新作的“生活系统是无限的，因此只要你愿意，你可以一直玩下去”。当一名与会者评论说 神鬼寓言4 “不是一款大作”时，Littler 再次澄清道，“如果你想的话，你真的可以永远玩下去。”
作为对比，完美主义玩家通常在第一部游戏中花费约 30 小时来完成全收集，在第二和第三部中则需要约 50 小时。神鬼寓言4 似乎延续了这一趋势，但在明年 Playground 和 Xbox 将游戏交到玩家手中之前，我们还无法窥见其全貌。
神鬼寓言4 目前定于 2027 年 2 月 23 日在 PC、PlayStation 5 和 Xbox Series X/S 平台上发布。在 2020 年 7 月首次公布六年后，总监 Ralph Fulton 表示，他很高兴看到这款游戏与许多其他作品一同发布，并且庆幸 GTA6 不在其中。

items.title: GTA6 玩家认为他们在现实中找到了杰森与露西亚在罪恶都市的公寓

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/cwpcbhbubjDtbib.png
GTA6 粉丝认为他们已经找到了杰森和露西亚在罪恶都市公寓的现实生活原型——但别指望能亲自去参观。
GTA6
动作冒险, 角色扮演
PC 玩家们，我知道你们很急，但你们先 别 急。
查看更多 立即下载
Grand Theft Auto V 传承版 玩家一次又一次地证明了他们会竭尽全力去挖掘 Rockstar Games 作品中最微小的细节，对于 GTA6 也是如此。就在大规模加长演示展示了杰森和露西亚在罪恶都市的公寓几天后，一位观察者自发地去寻找迈阿密现实生活中似乎相同的公寓。
Instagram 用户 prettyboycuh 是第一个公开分享该位置的人，他表示自己首先使用谷歌地图寻找上周实机预告片中首次出现的一栋青色高层建筑。他说“这很简单”，但当他使用街景功能转向杰森和露西亚公寓所在地时，他发现的只有一片草地。接着，他回溯了时间。

他——你现在也可以亲自去查看——将地图的时间跨度从 2026 年 3 月更改为 2013 年 4 月，即 GTA 5 发布前约四个月，瞧，公寓出现了。Rockstar 尚未正式确认这座被称为 Belmar Condominium 的建筑就是我们在 GTA6 中看到杰森和露西亚挂靠地点的灵感来源，但相似之处实在难以忽视。颜色相同，围栏相同，周围的许多建筑也相同，我们甚至能看到杰森在加长演示中驶出的停车场。那么，它去哪了？
调查发现，这栋建筑一直存在到 2017 年，随后它的三文鱼色被重新喷涂成了深灰色。它在谷歌地图上一直显示到 2022 年，而 2024 年的记录显示，这个迈阿密地点已完全消失。
prettyboycuh 更进一步，发现了一份来自《南佛罗里达商业期刊》的报告，称 Belmar Condo 在 2022 年以 1200 万美元的总价售出。同一份报告指出，该建筑建于 1973 年，最终在收购后的某个时间被拆除。换句话说，如果你是想要参观杰森和露西亚故事中最具辨识度地点之一的 GTA6 粉丝，那你运气不太好。
尽管如此，你至今仍能通过谷歌地图看到该地点，prettyboycuh 还发现 Rockstar 也不经意地给粉丝留下了更多可看的内容。存档的 Zillow 房产列表显示，开发商在绘制公寓外部时不仅非常彻底，内部也是如此。从我们看到杰森从冰箱里拿饮料、看电视以及他的着装未能给露西亚留下深刻印象的简短片段来看，他们的公寓与现实中的灵感来源非常吻合。
GTA6 在上周四展示了约 27 分钟的游戏实机画面，如果玩家们现在的挖掘程度已经到了这种地步，那么当游戏真正发售时，社区会是什么样子就不得而知了。此前，粉丝们曾（错误地）从星象中寻找暗示，而另一些人则做得有些过火。当游戏于 2026 年 11 月 19 日在 PlayStation 5 和 Xbox Series X/S 上发售时，我们都能重返罪恶都市。

盘点所有基于布兰登·桑德森史诗级文学宇宙的 Cosmere 桌面游戏

others.title: 每一款 Cosmere 桌面游戏均基于布兰登·桑德森的史诗图书宇宙

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/XvwUoububjAdzxx.jpg
布兰登·桑德森的 Cosmere 宇宙自二十多年前他的第一部小说《伊岚翠》出版以来，一直令读者着迷。如今，该系列已涵盖 20 多本书，还有更多作品正在创作中，甚至根据极受欢迎的《迷雾之子》和《飓光志》系列改编的新电影和电视剧也即将问世。多年来，纹、卡拉丁和阿多纳西碎片的传说也从书页跃升到了桌面，多款棋盘游戏和桌面角色扮演游戏已经发布供玩家体验。
这份清单展示了你目前可以体验的所有桌面游戏，以及我们所知道的即将推出的作品！
The Brotherwise Games
Brotherwise Games 是 怪物领主、Night of the Ninja 和 Call to Adventure 等游戏的出版商，该工作室是桑德森 Cosmere 宇宙在棋盘游戏领域的官方合作伙伴。到目前为止，他们已经发布了多款作品，涵盖了几乎所有年龄段的 Cosmere 粉丝，而一些重磅作品仍在筹备中。
怪物领主
魔幻, 角色扮演, 半Q版, 2D, 即时, 单人, 多人, 跨平台联机游戏, 一次性付费
查看更多 立即下载
Call to Adventure: The Stormlight Archive

Call to Adventure: The Stormlight Archive 基于 Brotherwise 的 Call to Adventure 棋盘游戏系统，要求玩家创建出他们能想象到的最史诗、最有趣的角色。这是一款带有引擎构建要素的游戏，你将通过抽取卡牌来构建角色的历史、动机和命运，同时平衡他们的道德观，最终完成你个人的英雄之旅并获得评分。通过投掷精美的符文石来完成任务，在三个回合中游走于英雄与反英雄的界限之间，最终获胜者是拥有最传奇/最精彩角色背景故事（即得分最高）的玩家。这不仅是一款扎实的游戏，也是一次出色的角色构建练习，非常适合下一款游戏……
Cosmere RPG

对于桌面角色扮演游戏玩家来说，Cosmere RPG 为你提供了在柔夏世界中实现梦想的工具和系统。无论你是想走上成为光辉骑士的道路，还是化身为一名咏者，或者只是一个试图生存的普通士兵，Cosmere RPG 都能为你提供实现这一切的工具。你角色的动机以及你和朋友在 Cosmere 中创造的故事是这个系统的核心驱动力。Brotherwise 才刚刚起步，斯卡德里亚世界及其熔金术师也即将推出。目前已有一系列产品可供选择，包括包含在柔夏运行战役所需一切的 Stormlight Handbook，用于体验构建故事的 Stonewalkers Adventure，如果你只想浅尝辄止，还有一个入门套件 Cosmere RPG Starter Set。
Mistborn: The Deck Building Game

Mistborn: The Deck Building Game 展示了《迷雾之子》系列第一部《最后帝国》中的事件和角色，让 1-4 名玩家扮演包括纹和凯西尔在内的心爱角色。玩家将从可用的卡牌池中构建自己的牌组，同时学习并提高他们作为熔金术师（斯卡德里亚世界的标志性魔法）燃烧金属的能力。与此同时，玩家要努力变得足够强大以完成任务并击败其他玩家，或者在可选的合作游戏模式中挑战统御者本人。这款游戏拥有精美的艺术图和扎实的牌组构建核心，是《迷雾之子》粉丝的理想选择，而且很快就会推出扩展包，增加新角色、能力以及第二部小说 The Well of Ascension 中的精彩瞬间！
Shards of Creation

作为 Brotherwise 推出的三款主要 Cosmere 游戏中体量最轻的一款，Shards of Creation 是一款吃墩类卡牌游戏，根据选择的阿多纳西碎片（Shards of Adonalsium）的不同，你的玩法会发生很大变化。基础游戏中包含的每个碎片：Autonomy、Cultivation、Devotion、Dominion、Honor、Odium、Preservation 和 Ruin 都拥有独特的能力，在你为终局评分组合花色时，这些能力既能帮助你也可能阻碍你。游戏中包含了碎片承载者的官方形象描写（至少到目前为止是这样），其中一些是首次在 Shards of Creation 中亮相，这使得它不仅是 Cosmere 粉丝的绝佳选择，也适合那些只想在闲暇时间玩上一局优秀的吃墩游戏的玩家。
经典旧作
在 Brotherwise 与桑德森建立合作伙伴关系之前，另一家出版商 Crafty Games 曾尝试将作者广受欢迎的《迷雾之子》系列改编为桌面游戏。
Mistborn: House War
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/WazsCvbubjAdBwE.jpg

Mistborn: House War 的背景设定在第一部小说期间，是一款资源管理游戏。玩家不再扮演特定角色的迷雾披风，而是扮演城市中的各个派系。目标是通过解决帝国周围的问题来平息动乱，竞争以赢得最多的青睐。这款游戏较少涉及金属燃烧和穿梭迷雾，更多的是关于达成交易，但 Mistborn: House War 有一个转折，即分数最低或最高的玩家都有可能获胜。规则还允许进行 60-90 分钟的短程游戏或两到三小时的长程游戏，为你和你的团队提供了灵活性，既可以作为填充游戏，也可以作为当晚的主力游戏。扩展包 The Siege of Luthadel 扩展了游戏内容，将背景设定在第二部小说期间，并试图维持一切不至于崩溃。
Mistborn Adventure Game
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/WCyjCIbubjAdDrj.jpg

作为首款设定在 Cosmere 世界的桌面角色扮演游戏，Mistborn Adventure Game 最初于 2012 年夏天发布。这个桌面冒险系统允许玩家在斯卡德里亚世界中创建 Nobels、Skaa、Terrismen 甚至 Kandra，在《迷雾之子》传奇的第一纪元体验他们的故事。该系统由 Crafty Games 开发，基于 d6 骰子，更加侧重叙事，命运（Destiny）和悲剧（Tragedy）等因素会影响角色创建。Mistborn Adventure Game 发布了一系列扩展包和附加书籍，包括专注于泰瑞司人和藏金术师的 Terris: Wrought of Copper，以及 Alloy of Law、Skaa: Tin & Ash、Alloy of Law: Masks of the past 和 Nobels: The Golden Mandate。
即将推出
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260831/rSkpWBbubjAevqE.png
如果你还意犹未尽，Brotherwise Games 在未来一段时间内应该能满足你对 Cosmere 桌面游戏的需求，多款游戏和扩展包即将面世。《迷雾之子》牌组构建游戏迎来了它的第一个扩展包 The Well of Ascension，其特色是全新的合作模式，玩家需要共同努力保护卢瑟戴尔城免受克罗司大军的进攻，还有更多内容取自《迷雾之子》第二纪元的第二本书。
继续熔金术之旅，Cosmere RPG 很快也将推出其《迷雾之子》相关书籍，让玩家创建自己的迷雾之子和熔金术师，同时参与设定在该系列第一纪元和第二纪元的冒险！
最后，在今年秋天晚些时候，Brotherwise 将把《飓光志》系列带到 Kickstarter，推出他们的 War for Roshar 棋盘游戏。这是一款重度的区域控制/德式策略游戏，最多四名玩家将代表 Honor 或 Odium 阵营进行对抗，努力占领誓门（Oathgates），并扭转战争局势使其对自己有利。

这次的全新预告片展示了大量实机画面，画面品质相较前作有了极大幅度的提升，整体效果更加拟真，NPC角色也更加灵动，没有那种生硬的假人感，这个水平绝对对得起玩家的期待。

en......有点呼吸困难了。

本作作为九阴IP续作，采用单机开放世界制作模式，和2012年上线的初代网游形成明显区别。
早期《九阴真经》网游在国产网游品类中就算是非常独特的一个，不知道这次跟随国单潮流推出全新单机作品，是否会给玩家们带来更多的惊喜。
但有一说一，蜗牛的大饼太多了，游戏具体能不能做出来，效果又会如何，还得等具体发售才能知道。

content.v: Star Wars Galaxies Legends, one of many community servers offering a version of the defunct MMO with custom additions, reportedly had its assets decrypted by a hacker with the username levarrishawk (via Massively OP ). In a post on the Star Wars Galaxies subreddit, Levarris confirmed the details of a Discord post shared by the server's development team.

"[W]e’ve confirmed that Levarris, aka levarrishawk from r/swg, used AI tools to decrypt our client side game asset files," the Discord post reads. "This gave him access to assets from all of our custom content: items, questlines … We do know that he’s actively offered these files to other servers, and while we can’t confirm that he’s had any takers yet, if you start seeing Legends‑exclusive content out in other worlds it was likely taken from us.
"We’re obviously bothered by this, but there isn’t much we can do outside of being upfront with all of you and staying focused on what makes Legends great."

Notably, no player data or personal info was accessed. The response from Levarris, who is a moderator for the Star Wars Galaxies subreddit, reveals the motivation behind this hack: some drama that goes back "roughly fourteen years ago."

Levarris claims that some folks who'd eventually work on Legends used a "honeypot" scheme to acquire dev tools that Sony Online Entertainment used when working on the live game, and then didn't share those tools with other community devs trying to revive it. "You don't get to protect and hoard from the greater community things built on stolen goods," Levarris wrote.

The subreddit didn't seem impressed with the stunt nor the rationale behind it. "I’m just trying to play around with a lightsaber after working 60 hours in a week," commented iceman2kx. "A moderator of the Star Wars Galaxies subreddit has decided to actively harm the Star Wars Galaxies community at large. Cool. Cool and good," BroReesta wrote on the same thread.

items.summary: Choice and consequence vs. death and consequence.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ckZUwfxbakq5yXMJMfSmBW.png

Welcome to Dungeon Master , PC Gamer's regular RPG column, where Online Editor Fraser Brown delves into PC gaming's most beloved and enduring genre. This week, Associate Editor Ted Litchfield has subbed in to trade iron short swords and goblins for blaster rifles and clone troopers

When I first tried Star Wars Zero Company for preview, its rhythm reminded me quite a bit of Mass Effect 2: Walk around your home base, upgrade stuff, talk to people, select non-combat activities and missions from a galaxy map, and enter levels that feel "strictly business." Heavy on the combat, with minimal nonviolent gameplay.

It really struck me that Zero Company evolved into this form that has a lot of appeal for the story-heavy RPG fan like myself, but emerged out of a very different, tactics game lineage. That process of reverse-engineering something very RPG-like from a separate but related genre has resulted in a game that I'm not sure the likes of Owlcat, Obsidian, or Larian ever would have made.

Zero Company lacks the branching dialogue trees and minute reactivity of many RPGs, but taking on the apparently herculean task of making even story-centric characters permanently killable has resulted in a game that feels more profoundly reactive and personal than most RPGs I've ever played.
Consequential

One of the coolest things about Zero Company is its simultaneous embrace of permanently missable/killable/losable main characters and triple-A production values, something I think I've only otherwise seen in Baldur's Gate 3, and there only through specific beats of the main story.

In Zero Company, if an operator gets knocked down three times without a stay at the medbay in-between, they're gone for good, no ifs, ands, or buts. Unless you tweak the setting in the game's difficulty—but come on, don't do that. Save scum like a true PC gamer.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bvKeFfpZpQycABsMUzGDnC.jpg

Zero Company's focus on tactical combat as its north star means you don't see other forms of RPG choice and consequence, like alienating people out of your party in BG3 or Rogue Trader, but being able to permanently miss out on a companion's presence and subplot due to a careless mistake in combat feels more meaningful and personal than many of the authored choices in games I love.

There are very few RPGs that have managed to truly paralyze me with their binary moral choices⁠— Dread Delusion and Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty spring to mind⁠—but more often, I feel fairly secure in the choices I make in such games, and even stick with them in subsequent playthroughs.

But a true sense of consequence can make things pop even if I know what I want to stick with. Being a commie in Disco Elysium is made richer by the very existence of its fascist playthrough, knowing how dark and depressing the story can get. Kim Kitsuragi's trust and friendship means so much more when you understand it's possible to lose it. Baldur's Gate 3's happiest endings feel almost saccharine to me, but I don't mind, because the bad guy endings are so grim. You have to really work to keep everybody alive by the final party.

Zero Company's companion questlines are excellent, and clone trooper Trick's in particular blew me away. The fact that I have to work to keep Trick alive and see that story makes it feel more my own, even if someone else sees the exact same thing. Bit Reactor has made systemic and authored storytelling compliment each other in a truly novel, rare way. The Fire Emblem series has managed something similar, but not at this level of production values (full voice acting!) or with a cast so closely intertwined with the main plot.
Loss leader
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2XtUvqUuiDEz5BshsYnKd7.jpg

If there's anything I want Bit Reactor to do next, it's to even more tightly wind the threat of permanent loss into the plot. It's not possible to piss off squadmates enough that they leave your crew through the Bond (approval) system in Zero Company. I would love to see that wrench thrown into things in Bit Reactor's next project.

There are story moments in Zero Company that genuinely imperil or drive away your companions: I want to see even more of that. Zero Company's permadeath is a unique melding of story and gameplay in the current field, but otherwise, the game's story and gameplay are fairly siloed from each other. The non-combat operations and exploration gameplay have fairly limited effects on the story and tactical side of things: You take on a mission, or you don't. You have access to new resources, or you lack them.

With more time, resources, and experience making this sort of game, I would love for Bit Reactor's next project to be even more of an RPG, to embrace consequence and reactivity even more deeply. It's already a phenomenal first outing , and I can't wait to see what's next.

items.title: 《全面战争：战锤 40,000》荣获科隆游戏展最佳 PC 游戏奖
items.summary: Previews of the grimdark strategy game are turning heads.

content.v: When Total War: Warhammer first debuted, I was much more into the wargame setting's sci-fi counterpart. This would be cool if Space Marines were in it , I remember thinking, somehow unaware that Total War: Warhammer would end up being one of the best strategy games on PC . Not that my theory was wrong: Space Marines are finally in Total War, and it is, in fact, cool. Just ask the folks who picked this year's Gamescom award winners: it won best PC game .

It's the third award Sega took home this year, along with best audio for Alien: Isolation 2 and best lineup for its whole gaggle of games. It's easy to see why, particularly in the case of Total War 40K—PC Gamer's Fraser Brown said it took a mere hour of playtime to cement the game as the highlight of his year . "It's immediately obvious how special Total War 40k is—I don't think a tutorial has ever made me giddy before," he wrote.

According to Gamescom's website, the winners are chosen "by both an expert jury of gaming professionals and the community." In other words, it was a favorite among both professional nerds and the pro bono sort.

If it wasn’t clear before why people have been so vocally insistent that this game should happen ever since Total War first embraced fantasy, it should be now: there are many ways to adapt Warhammer 40,000's galaxy-spanning eternal war in videogame form, but Total War's combination of scale and gruesome, exacting detail seems a particularly good fit.

Warhammer thrives on extremes, and a game where I can watch a single ultramarine hack an ork to bits up close then immediately zoom out to see an enormous whirlwind of violence in wide shot is an exciting prospect indeed. As for whether that'll pan out into a good game once it finally releases, we'll have to wait and see.

items.title: 得益于专门团队对每个 NPC 进行“艺术指导”，GTA 6 的独特动画数量是 GTA 5 的 10 倍以上

content.v: There are big-budget blockbusters, and then there's GTA 6. If you want any sense of just how big this thing is, look no further than a recent interview Rockstar North co-head Aaron Garbut gave The New York Times (via Techradar ). In it, he said the studio dedicated an entire new team solely to making NPCs.

"We art-directed each individual one of them," Garbut said in the interview. "Every room in the game, somebody thought about this … Who's sitting where, what they're drinking, the marks that are left on the table. The pictures on the wall will have the people that are in that room, with their tattoos on their arms and their family behind them.

"That whole thing has been made, and built, and photographed, and placed in this random room in a random building in a huge city, in a world." He revealed that GTA 6 has over 600,000 animations—double the amount Red Dead Redemption 2 had, both of which dwarf GTA 5's 55,000. Considering the game's map is also three times as big as Red Dead 2's, it seems like the game operates on an unprecedented level of scale and fidelity.

This all lines up with what PC Gamer's US editor-in-chief Tyler Wilde said of the game in the wake of recent leaks earlier this month : even if GTA 6 doesn't reinvent the open world crime-'em-up, it "will be impressive for the same reason Rockstar games typically are: The absurd amount of effort and money the studio puts into making them as big and detailed as the mainstream hardware of the day can manage."

items.title: 《Elden Ring》的黯淡版本身就足够令人兴奋，但这也是我们正确体验游戏发布日宣传的最后机会
items.summary: One last hurrah for "fort comma night," "Mist, or Beast," and "offer pickle."

content.v: Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.

Elden Ring is one of the best videogames I've ever played, and now, four years from launch, is possibly the last time you'll get to experience it as an event . The Tarnished Edition DLC looks small on paper⁠—two new classes and a smattering of armor and items⁠—but it is still something new, something unexpected added to our 2022 game of the year.

What in any other context might make for a Horse Armor -style embarrassment is one of the most exciting releases of 2026 for me, and I'm only, like, a quarter joking. Elden Ring is the type of game that made a couple borked quests getting patched into a massive communal treasure hunt . New weapons, armor, and classes at this late date feels like a profound gift, even if I'm paying for the privilege.

But, in addition to the material additions coming to Elden Ring, the Tarnished Edition DLC serves as an enticement to the playerbase, something to bring them back all at one time and bring life back to the Lands Between's ailing multiplayer invasions and co-operative boss battling.

I still remember how magical the first days of Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree were, the density of asynchronous messages and ease of matchmaking. The Tarnished Edition won't be able to match either of those highs, but its launch may represent the biggest spike in player activity we could ever expect to see in Elden Ring again.

If you've somehow missed the boat on this one since 2022, I envy the first experience you're about to have. Elden Ring's fantasy is somehow both mythic and anthropological, zoomed out, and deeply personal.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/FL6XTFLKhXvQLrVMjtzqvE.jpg

You're an anonymous warrior on a quest to become God's Husband (gender-agnostic). The God in question is a man and woman, separate but the same, consubstantial with, and plotting against themselves. Her pope is a giant turtle , and she is perpetuating a millennia-old conflict involving both racial animus and metaphysics. You can make her goth half- (single? step?) daughter God instead if you so choose.

It's all set in a world of literally impossible beauty, one of the best fantasy settings ever rendered in a videogame. It's dominated by the alien, iconic view of the Erdtree, an ethereal, skyscraper-sized growth that's visible from every part of the Lands Between. Elden Ring is, perhaps, one of FromSoftware's most bright and cheerful creations to date, but it's also one of the weirdest. In four years, it's lodged itself into my psyche like almost no game world I've ever seen.

But enough about all that nerd stuff: FromSoft had already ruined all other 3D action games for me by the time Elden Ring came out, and while it lacks the pure focus of Sekiro's perfect block symphony , I think it matches that more straightforward action game as a fantasy combat experience. Elden Ring is one of the broadest, deepest, and most exquisitely designed action-RPGs that's ever been made.

It even contains Sekiro in a limited sense: One of the character build options added in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is a perfect block mechanic lifted straight out of the ninja sim. Like no other game I've played, Elden Ring balances mechanically pure "it's your fault if you die" combat with a myriad of class fantasies and character build options. Knights, barbarians, spellcasters, rogues, priests, samurai, nude men with earthenware hats, you can inhabit any of these roles while engaging in some of the tightest, richest, and most challenging action combat put to silicon.

Which, funnily enough, feeds back into the relatively small additions of the Tarnished Edition DLC: When the mechanics in play are this good, with so much already up in the air, even a minute adjustment feels momentous. FromSoft has not released a full-fledged, solo/async experience like Elden Ring, since Elden Ring, and until it shows off what it's working on next, the Tarnished Edition release will be the closest thing we have to playing a new FromSoft joint at launch.

I have a love/hate/hate relationship with Elden Ring Nightreign , which also no longer seems to be getting updates. In addition to being a Switch 2 exclusive, FromSoft's upcoming Duskbloods looks to have more in common with Nightreign than Bloodborne, firmly in the realm of " a multiplayer thing ." PCG contributor Tyler Colp's sense of FOMO withered on actually playing the game, and mine is rapidly following suit. With no FromSoft fix on the horizon to truly tickle my fancy, I can only turn, once again, to the Lands Between.

items.title: 14 年过去了，DayZ 的创造者仍在寻找生存游戏最大问题的解决方案：“我想如果不解决这个问题我就会死”

content.v: You might think making one of the most influential games of this century would be a source of unending happiness for its creator. But for Dean 'Rocket' Hall, founder of RocketWerkz, the relationship with his most famous creation isn't that simple. "When DayZ happened, it was like dying," says Hall of the mod which, alongside Minecraft, helped establish survival games as a cornerstone of the medium. "It ended my old life. My relationship with everyone who I knew up to that point changed completely."

This isn't to say Hall doesn't recognise his good fortune: "It was obviously an amazing thing that happened to me," he stresses. But there is a sense that, while Hall gained much from the creation of DayZ—fame, respect, and to a certain extent, fortune—something was lost too. "I loved making the mod, and I loved that feeling, and I've been chasing it ever since."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CHt5cPwxLdboAPMsLCikU7.jpg

Chasing the feeling of making DayZ has taken over a decade, sent Hall down numerous rabbit holes and even led his studio to the precipice of bankruptcy. After all that time, Hall still hasn't found what he is looking for and admits he may never find it. Yet as he continues his search, RocketWerkz is beginning to find success on its own terms.
Hall of fame

What is it, exactly, that would rekindle the feeling of making DayZ for Hall? Specifically, he says he's searching for a solution to a specific problem he sees in survival games. "You see it time [and] again. If you go see commentary on a survival game, people will say it gets boring, or the end game sucks," he says. "And it's such a hard problem, because what you do [to] solve it [is] brute force it with heaps of content."

It's not clear when exactly Hall identified this issue, but it was likely between RocketWerkz's first and second released games. When the DayZ mod launched, Hall was working at Bohemia Interactive, the creators of ArmA 2 which served as the original basis for DayZ.

This wasn't the first mod Hall had made for ArmA 2. Indeed, it was modding that landed Hall his job at Bohemia, after his co-op mod for ArmA 2 became the most popular mod on the defunct ArmA fansite Armaholic. Despite running a major video game developer, Hall still regularly makes mods today for games like RimWorld and Barotrauma .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/aUFPL2vK2qgohEKQdJbfTK.jpg

"People think I'm a game developer who came up from [being] a modder, and I would say I'm a modder who makes games during the day," Hall explains. "I was born a modder and I will die a modder. And I think if there's a lesson out there for any aspiring game devs, I think it's mod games. You will learn even faster than making them."

DayZ's surging popularity led Bohemia Interactive to begin creating a commercial version of the mod. Hall initially led the project, but he left Bohemia in 2014, which is when he founded RocketWerkz and began work on a project called Ion.

Ion would later be cancelled, with RocketWerkz pivoting to Stationeers , a space-station construction and management game inspired by one of Hall's favourite games, Space Station 13. Yet when it was released in 2017, Stationeers received mixed reviews, and has struggled commercially throughout its existence. "It's built up about seven years of losses," Hall says, though he adds that in 2025 it "actually probably broke even."
Close to the sun

While well received by players, Stationeers struggled commercially and remains in Steam early access. Following Stationeers, RocketWerkz began developing Icarus , a free-to-play, online survival game with a run-based loop. Players would land on a planet, go through the basic survival loop while completing an objective, launch back into space, and begin another mission that would start the cycle again.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/9tuwASdDrD4wPEwKbfCUPR.jpg

This was Hall's attempt to solve that problem of survival games running out of road. But there were two problems. First, players didn't like the loop, as they perceived it as losing progress. "It just didn't work. People didn't want it. It was hilarious, but that's life."

Second, on launch, Icarus was not the financial success that RocketWerkz needed it to be to survive. As such, RocketWerkz pivoted quickly, abandoning the free-to-play aspect and committing to a rigorous post-launch support scheme where it would release weekly updates like clockwork. "After the beta weekend, I levelled with the team. I was like 'We do this or it's over.' We might even do all this work and still go bankrupt, " he says. Hall is open about how gruelling a process this was. "The last couple of years, I've been enjoying it, but before that, I hated it, and we were looking at ruin, basically."

Nonetheless, Icarus has slowly established a trusting audience, one which RocketWerkz could then sell larger, paid expansions to. "Icarus, at times, we can have a 50% attachment rate to DLC at purchase," Hall explains. "I can tell you right now, the studio would be bankrupt if we didn't do that strategy."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/3LwJ6LUqujwAGCWL7b3cqf.jpg

Yet even here, the margins can be slim. "People will go and say: 'There's too many DLC, this is crazy'. And I'll post our financials. I'll be like 'Hey, a lot of our DLC, even on Icarus— which is really good—sometimes we'll only make $100,000 from it. It might have cost us $120,000 to make. So we're not printing money."

Indeed, Hall says that it's only in the last year that Icarus has really begun making money. "We've increased our revenue 80% in the last year," he says. "Our dream for a long time has been to make more per day than we spend, because as a game developer, you need to build a big cash reserve, especially now because there's no investment money out there."
Rocket purr-kz

The experience of making Icarus has taught Hall a lot. He says he's learned the value of community, how a relatively small audience can be more valuable than hundreds of thousands of players—provided the audience is dedicated enough. "My encouragement to devs is: focus on getting fans, not on selling product."

He also believes a small audience can be just as emotionally gratifying as a large one. "I think seeing that 100 people love what you do is chemically the same as 100,000 at least," Hall elaborates. "If you're a musician [like] Freddie Mercury and you pack out the Wembley Stadium, seeing 100,000 people right there waving lighters is probably insane. But as a Game Dev, I don't know whether there's as big a difference. So if I can make a mod that 100 people love, that's like crack cocaine to me."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WJR5MsfMu5GgxnjJsvF6cW.jpg

It was this line of thinking that informed RocketWerkz' approach with Kitten Space Agency —the studio's freely available spiritual successor to Kerbal Space Program, a game which Hall personally adores. "With Kitten Space Agency, the game is completely free. It's funded entirely by contributions. So that really puts it in front of the gamer's face," he says. "If you want this game to exist, how much is it worth? Because it's all on you."

While letting players determine the value of a game has its own risks, Hall likes it as a funding model, saying it absolves him of the need to justify a price point, and allows him to focus on the creative aspect: "I think if I could, I would just do all my games for free, because it stops you having to be focused on dumb stuff, and allows you to focus on the good stuff, which is what you get to do for modding."

content.v: Retro gaming is just regular gaming to a sick, twisted mind like mine (and that of everyone I know, since we spend all our time playing old crap ). But what makes something retro in the first place? Is it bits? Console generation? The size and contents of the box it came in, assuming it came in one at all? Whatever it is, it seems like the Wii and PS3 are being grandfathered into the definition—at least on Game Center CX, a Japanese retro gaming TV show.

According to an article from Automaton Media , the show—which is essentially a let's play variety show starring comedian Shinya Arino—recently held a vote as to whether Wii and PS3 games should be awarded the "retro" moniker and considered for inclusion. The poll reportedly got over 14,000 responses with 71% voting in favor, and when a second round followed, that percentage rose to 80% among nearly 17,000 voters. Arino declared that games from both consoles will indeed be considered for the show moving forward.

So what does this have to do with PC gaming? Well, we have a retro gaming scene too, and if we agree for the sake of argument that those consoles are retro on the basis that they're turning 20 this year, that would mean the following PC games are also retro: Medieval II: Total War, Half-Life 2: Episode One, Dawn of War - Dark Crusade, Neverwinter Nights 2, the first season of Telltale's Sam & Max reboot, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, and perhaps most upsettingly, Company of Heroes.

Personally, I think it'd be a lot more fruitful to split our medium's history into distinct eras—something like console generations, but maybe less arbitrary than those divisions are—but it's also fun to have a label that gets thrown around once we've all agreed something is for old fuddy-duddies.

In that sense, I think the Wii and PS3 completely fit, even it's hard to swallow the notion of The Last of Us as being a game that debuted on "retro" hardware. Still, it's hard to imagine that definition will be useful for very long (if it is even of any use now). In 2046 are we going to say GTA 6 is a retro game, as if it has much of anything in common with games we hold as undeniably retro now, like Excitebike or DuckTales?

items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartm

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/30/gta-6-jason-and-lucia-apartment-1788107138247.png
Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartment – but don't expect to ever visit it yourself.

Grand Theft Auto players have proven time and time again that they will go to the ends of the earth to learn the smallest details about Rockstar Games experiences, and that hasn't changed for GTA 6. Just days after the big extended look presentation revealed Jason and Lucia's apartment in Vice City, one watcher took it upon themselves to hunt down what appears to be the same apartment in real-life Miami.

Instagram user prettyboycuh was the first to publicly share the location, saying they started by using Google Maps to find a tall teal building that was first shown in last week's gameplay trailer. They said "that was easy," but when they used the Street View function to turn to where Jason and Lucia's apartment should be, all they found was a patch of grass. Then, they turned back the clock.

They – and you can still see this for yourself, too – changed the map's time period from March 2026 to April 2013, around four months before the launch of GTA 5 , and voila, the apartment appeared. Rockstar hasn't officially confirmed what was known as the Belmar Condominium to be the inspiration for the spot we see Jason and Lucia hanging out at in GTA 6, but the similarities are too difficult to ignore. It's the same color, has the same fence, many of the buildings around it are the same, and we can even see the parking lot Jason pulled out of in the extended look. So, where'd it go?

IGN replicated prettyboycuh's findings and can report that the building stuck around through 2017 before it was repainted from its salmon color to some darker grays. It shows up on Google Maps through 2022 before a 2024 recording shows that the Miami location completely vanished.

prettyboycuh took things one step further and found a report from the South Florida Business Journal stating that The Belmar Condo was sold for a total of $12 million in 2022. The same report stated the building was established in 1973 before it was eventually demolished sometime after the buyout. In other words, if you're a GTA 6 fan looking to visit what could become one of the most recognizable locations in Jason and Lucia's story, you're out of luck.

Still, you can see the location through Google Maps to this day, and prettyboycuh discovered that Rockstar inadvertently gave fans more to gawk at, too. Archived Zillow listings show the developer was not only thorough when mapping the outside of the apartment but the inside, too. From the brief glimpses we see of Jason grabbing drinks from the fridge, watching TV, and failing to impress Lucia with his outfit choices, it looks like their apartment pretty closely matches the real-life inspiration.

GTA 6 gave fans about 27 minutes of in-game footage last Thursday, and if this is the length players are going to already, there's no telling what the community will be like when the game actually launches. Previously, fans have (incorrectly) looked to the stars for hints , while others have taken things a bit too far . We'll all be able to revisit Vice City when it launches November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Be sure to also learn about what GTA 6 won't have at launch and the streamer who believes Rockstar designed a character based on himself . IGN recently got to learn a lot about the new Grand Theft Auto, but you can check out just 99 of our favorite details here . Our preview and interview are both also available for those looking to learn more.
